deities: Sri Siddharoodha Swami (samadhi shrine; marble statue)

history.summary: Monastic institution (math) at Srinivasa Nagar, Old Hubli (Karwar Road), built around the samadhi of the Advaita saint Sri Siddharoodha Swami (born 1836/1837; took samadhi 2 August 1929), who settled in Hubli in 1877. The samadhi mandir was built 1897-1907; the complex houses a marble statue of the Swami and propagates his Advaita teaching of universal brotherhood. It was visited by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1919) and Mahatma Gandhi (1924). The annual car festival is held on Maha Shivaratri. NOTE: this is a Hindu math/samsthana (a saint's samadhi shrine), not a conventional temple structure - keep-or-drop decision for a temples dataset. Sources differ on the saint's birth year (1836 vs 1837) and on daily hours (6 AM-6 PM vs 4 AM-9 PM).

town_description: Hubli (officially Hubballi), twin city with Dharwad, is the largest city in North Karnataka and a major commercial and transport hub. It is noted for spiritual centres such as the Siddharoodha Math.
